obstruction.where: the intermediate layers j >= 2 of the smooth descent in Analysis/Sard/Smooth.lean (critical_subset_layers, exists_flat_direction, exists_local_graph)
obstruction.mechanism: on the layer where derivatives of order <= j vanish and order j+1 does not, the descent restricts u to the regular zero set of a j-th derivative component w; for u in C^n, w and the graph chart are C^(n-j) and so is the restriction u∘ψ (diagnostic D1), but the induction hypothesis in dimension n-1 needs C^(n-1)
obstruction.loss: j-1 derivatives; j = 1 is exactly enough, j >= 2 fails; consistent with the 2026-09-15 finding that n = 4, j = 2 is the first uncovered case
obstruction.consequence: any route that restricts u first and then descends in dimension pays this; changing the stratification does not help

route.name: Morse (1939) decomposition of an arbitrary set, C^k formulation after Norton (1994)
references: A. P. Morse, The behavior of a function on its critical set, Ann. of Math. 40 (1939) 62-70
A. Norton, The Zygmund Morse-Sard theorem, J. Geom. Anal. 4 (1994) 403-424
A. Sard, The measure of the critical values of differentiable maps, Bull. AMS 48 (1942) 883-890
H. Whitney, A function not constant on a connected set of critical points, Duke Math. J. 1 (1935) 514-517 (sharpness; not in scope)

objects.disk: a C^1 map phi : Fin p -> R  ->  Fin n -> R, antilipschitz on the closed unit ball; body phi '' closedBall 0 1; the parametric segment from phi a to phi b is the image of [a,b]
objects.flat_of_order_k_along_a_disk_on_S: for all eps > 0 there is delta > 0 such that for a, b in the unit ball with phi a, phi b in S and |phi a - phi b| < delta, |f (phi (a + s(b-a)))| <= eps |phi a - phi (a + s(b-a))|^k for s in [0,1]
objects.morse_decomposition_of_order_k_of_A: a countable set A0 and countably many pieces carried by disks covering A such that every C^k function vanishing on A is flat of order k along each piece

double_induction.k = 0: uniform continuity on the compact body
double_induction.k -> k+1 at fixed n (critical part): split A into U (every C^(k+1) function vanishing on A is critical on U) and V; on U the coordinates of fderiv f are C^k, vanish on U, hence flat of order k by the order-k decomposition of U, and M2 raises the order
double_induction.n -> n+1 at fixed k (regular part): near a point of V some C^k function vanishing on A has nonzero differential, so V lies locally on a C^k graph over n coordinates (M1); apply the n-dimensional hypothesis at the SAME k to the preimage and push forward along the 1-antilipschitz graph map (M1'); second countability makes countably many local decompositions suffice

route.why_no_regularity_is_lost: the induction hypothesis quantifies over all sets at a fixed order k; what is restricted to a graph is never u but the class of C^k functions vanishing on A, which stays C^k on the graph
route.finish: M4 (criticality lemma) forgets the disks; M5 applies the proved covering count volume_image_eq_zero_of_oscillation_pow with exponent n = k+1 on each bounded piece; M6 transports along ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq exactly as sard_smooth does
